input_population.note: Both pools read unmodified; not reconstructed for this audit.

resources_evaluated.type: A. Static lexicon w/ per-term context annotation

excluded_not_reproducible.reason: deliberately not sought or constructed for safety/dual-use-scope reasons

hurtlex_raw_matching.note: case-insensitive substring match, both levels (conservative+inclusive), all 17 categories

hurtlex_collision_audited_matching.note: case-insensitive whole-word/phrase match (regex word boundaries), conservative level only

harmful_pool_hurtlex_category_breakdown_.note: remaining categories not itemized in the retained Markdown; these three are the only per-HurtLex-category counts recorded

counts_derivation_method: hit_n/zero_hit_n values are arithmetically back-derived from the published rate and n: each is the unique integer whose rate rounds to the published one-decimal-place value, cross-checked to sum to n. None were obtained by rerunning or rescoring.

limitations.per_source_topic_category_hit_rate_break: Observed qualitatively during the audit (ranged 68.8% to 100% under raw HurtLex matching, noisier under collision-audited matching for categories as small as n=2), but the underlying per-category computation was not retained as a separate artifact. Not reproduced here; treat the range as a qualitative observation, not an audited figure backed by retained data.

hurtlex_raw_matching.label: not_useful
hurtlex_raw_matching.basis: benign-control hit rate (85-88%) close to harmful-pool hit rate (96%); dominated by generic-token collisions

hurtlex_collision_audited_matching.label: supplementary_interpretable_signal
hurtlex_collision_audited_matching.basis: removes most raw-matching noise but harmful-pool hit rate (36.8%) does not exceed XSTest-safe (38.0%); no net discriminative value; diagnostic/auditing lens only

mol.label: supplementary_interpretable_signal
mol.basis: small real monotonic separation but coverage too sparse (12.9% hit rate, 0.16 hits/prompt) for a global or domain-limited primary signal

conclusion: HurtLex and MOL provide supplementary interpretable lexical signals, but neither supplies sufficiently broad and specific coverage for a global primary CUE measure. The next possible direction is a newly defined within-harmful lexical-outlierness pilot; the existing harmful-versus-benign TF-IDF+Logistic Regression and Fightin' Words machinery in src/cue_scoring.py and src/corpus_discrimination.py must not be reused as that measure without explicit redesign.
